reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports using displacement covariances to compute vibrational entropy in solids, including a HEA example, and notes the method works with AIMD ensembles. However, it does not address fluid phases, fusion free-energy differences, or the claimed order-of-magnitude speed-up, leaving key premises about fluid treatment and cost reduction unsupported.
premises: Vibrational entropy of solids can be accurately obtained from the covariance matrix of atomic displacements via a Gaussian approximation.
The covariance-based method works for elemental solids (Na, Al) and a high-entropy alloy (MoNbTaW).
The method requires only short AIMD trajectories to collect displacement ensembles.
The approach can be extended to fluid phases with similar statistical ensemble treatment.
The method yields entropy values in good agreement with experimental data above the Debye temperature.
